page: Amazon Web Services c4.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor running at 2.9 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 1.88 GB per core, and does not include local storage or GPU hardware. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate single-core capabilities alongside weaker multi-core and memory performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scores 1480.59, which is in the average tier, while the multi-core CPU score drops to a weak 3903.16. Memory bandwidth is relatively constrained, with read-only large block speeds at 25.92 GB/sec and write speeds at 22.39 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression at 24.42 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 9.13 GB/sec perform at average levels, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor at 17.33 GB/sec.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and AVX, AES, and FMA instruction support, the c4.xlarge is suited for compute-bound workloads that do not require high memory density or local storage. It achieves 1.64 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 3.51 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. For lightweight machine learning, it processes 135M model text generation at an average speed of 81.87 tokens/sec. The lack of bundled local storage and low memory-to-vCPU ratio represent clear tradeoffs, positioning this instance as a budget-friendly option for legacy compute tasks, basic web serving, and moderate single-threaded processing.

Operating on the Xen hypervisor, this x86_64 instance lacks local storage and GPU acceleration, relying on a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.
